text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed higher although origin offers shaved gains. March ended $20 higher at $1,652 per tonne, while May added $15 to close at $1,675 per tonne. Traders said London seemed more restrained in its action than New York, allowing the arbitrage between robusta and arabica widen to an extraordinary 105 cents/lb basis March from 40 cents in December.

Nerves were strained on Friday before a long weekend in the United States on Monday which traders said could leave the market vulnerable to profit taking. The price swings in London are not as pronounced as in New York because robustas are in greater supply than arabicas.

In New York arabica futures ended with modest losses after a spectacular climb much of the week which took the market to about 2 year highs. Traders said today's breather was light profit taking ahead of a long weekend, but that the uptrend is still intact as present levels are not sufficient to ration demand and there is simply not that much supply that could become available in the near term to halt the upward move.

The March/May switch, a barometer of near-term availability narrowed slightly to 10.85 cents/lb compared with 11.05 cents/lb at 14 February. March ended 2.20 cents/lb lower at 177.85 cents/lb, while May gave up 2.00 cents/lb to close at 167.00 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 1.40 to 2.95 cents/lb. The physical market remained extremely quiet, with roasters stepping aside after the steep rise in futures prices. Traders said CSCE, March's ballooning premium to second-month May also soured roasters appetite for the market, while producers were eager to price coffee against the spot contract.

COLOMBIA - Union leaders threatened on February 16 to step up a six-day-old state workers' strike by shutting down the key oil industry and calling on private sector employees to join in solidarity. The last round of talks aimed at ending the work stoppage by an estimated 800,000 public sector employees ended in a deadlock.

The government, battling to slash a gaping fiscal deficit, has so far rejected labour demands for a 21.5 per cent pay hike and an end to a planned wave of privatization. The strike is one of the largest labour movements since a civic stoppage in 1977, when at least 20 protesters were killed in a single day of riots in Bogota.

UNITED STATES - Maxwell House Coffee Co. said it will raise the list price of its standard ground 13-ounce can of coffee by 15 cents due to higher prices of green coffee on the world's futures market. The increase, which is to take effect on March 31, brings the new price for a standard can to $2.41, the company said.

CANADA - Canada imported 241,532 bags of coffee in October 1996, 6.8 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 2.279 million bags, nearly 12 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995.
Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 11 per cent to 2.510 million bags.

Main suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Mexico (221,300 vs 116,800 bags), Brazil (212,200 vs 229,000 bags) and Colombia (396,700 vs 304,100 bags). The country exported 283,800 bags of coffee in January/October 1996, 17 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 9 per cent to 303,800 bags.
